summary: Modern databases are converging AI/ML capabilities directly into the data layer, treating vectors as a native data type rather than requiring separate specialized stores — a shift reinforced by Gartner's forecast that 30%+ of enterprises will adopt vector databases by 2026 and that 75% of enterprise AI applications will depend on vector search. Platforms now bundle in-database LLM inference, embedding generation, semantic/hybrid retrieval, and classical ML (forecasting, anomaly detection, classification) so RAG and agentic workloads can run close to governed enterprise data. Purpose-built vector databases still have a role for extreme performance needs, but general-purpose multimodel engines (PostgreSQL ascendant, Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery) are absorbing most mainstream use cases.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, ML Functions)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless LLM functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), Cortex Search for hybrid semantic retrieval, Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL, and Document AI. Snowflake also made a ~$250M bet on Postgres (Crunchy Data acquisition) to bring transactional/live AI workflows into its AI Data Cloud alongside classical ML Functions for forecasting and anomaly detection.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a native VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY/VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions and the EMBED_TEXT family, plus the managed Cortex Search service for hybrid vector+keyword retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: First-party hosted LLMs (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, and others) callable via SQL/Python Cortex functions with no external API keys required; also integrates external models via Cortex Guard and Snowpark.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by compute warehouse plus per-token/per-query charges for Cortex LLM and Cortex Search functions; no separate license, costs scale with usage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML (in-SQL model training) + Vertex AI integration (generative AI & embeddings)
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series/ARIMA, boosted trees, DNNs) using standard SQL. Through Vertex AI integration it adds ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and remote model endpoints for generative AI and multimodal workloads directly over warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides a native VECTOR_SEARCH function with vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING for in-warehouse embedding generation.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI foundation models (Gemini, PaLM/text-embedding models) and remote model objects that call hosted or custom endpoints from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-as-you-go: on-demand bytes-scanned pricing or capacity-based slots, plus Vertex AI charges for generative/embedding model calls; BigQuery ML model training billed by data processed or flat-rate slots.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector (vector similarity) + pgai / pgvectorscale (embedding & LLM workflows)
databases.description: PostgreSQL has become 'ascendant' for AI because vectors are now just another column type alongside mature transactions, every ORM/driver, and SQL filtering. pgvector adds vector columns and ANN indexing, while the pgai extension brings embedding creation and LLM calls into SQL, and pgvectorscale improves ANN performance. Emerging engines (e.g. SynapCores) extend Postgres with EMBED() similarity, Cypher-style graph traversal, and in-database models like ANOMALY_SCORE.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not built into core PostgreSQL. Vector search is provided by the third-party pgvector extension (plus pgvectorscale/pgai); core Postgres has no native vector type, so capability depends on installing extensions.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension, which can generate embeddings and call LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama, etc.) directly from SQL; otherwise handled in the application layer.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; costs come from self-hosting infrastructure or managed providers (e.g. Timescale/Tiger, Supabase, Neon, AWS RDS/Aurora) that bill by compute and storage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (in-database SQL calls to SageMaker, Bedrock & Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML and generative AI models from SQL functions, passing row data to Amazon SageMaker endpoints, Amazon Bedrock foundation models, and Amazon Comprehend for sentiment/entity analysis — enabling inference (e.g. fraud scoring, recommendations) inline with transactional queries without moving data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is enabled via the pgvector extension (a third-party extension), not a built-in Aurora ML feature; Aurora ML focuses on model invocation, not vector indexing.
databases.llm_integration: Direct SQL-level integration with Amazon Bedrock foundation models (for generative text/embeddings) and SageMaker-hosted custom models.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage/I/O costs plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend usage charges for each inference call.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (CREATE MODEL in SQL via SageMaker Autopilot + Bedrock LLM integration)
databases.description: Redshift ML allows data warehouse users to create, train, and deploy ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, automatically leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot for training and hosting. It supports regression, classification, and bring-your-own-model workflows, and adds generative AI via integration with Amazon Bedrock LLMs from SQL, all over warehouse-scale data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively a vector search engine. Redshift ML centers on in-warehouse model training/inference; vector similarity is not a built-in Redshift ML capability (AWS steers vector-RAG workloads toward services like OpenSearch, Aurora/pgvector, or Bedrock Knowledge Bases).
databases.llm_integration: SQL-based integration with Amazon Bedrock foundation models for generative AI and with SageMaker for custom and auto-trained models.
databases.pricing_notes: No separate Redshift ML license; you pay standard Redshift compute/storage plus SageMaker training/hosting costs for CREATE MODEL and Bedrock inference charges for LLM calls.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) + Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides the end-to-end GenAI stack — model fine-tuning/training, Model Serving, Agent Framework, AI Gateway, and MLflow-based lifecycle management — unified with the Lakehouse. Databricks Vector Search delivers managed, automatically-synced vector indexes over Delta tables for RAG, governed by Unity Catalog.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed service that creates and auto-syncs vector indexes directly from Delta tables, with hybrid keyword+vector retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and AI Gateway host foundation models (Llama, DBRX, and others) and proxy external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic); Foundation Model APIs and ai_query() enable SQL/notebook LLM calls.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute, serving, and vector search, plus cloud infrastructure costs; Foundation Model APIs billed per token or via provisioned throughput.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search (native vector indexing) + Atlas AI integrations
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search embeds semantic similarity search directly into the document database, letting you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run $vectorSearch aggregation-pipeline queries. It supports approximate nearest-neighbor search and hybrid retrieval combining vector, full-text, and metadata filters for RAG and agentic applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability of MongoDB Atlas with a dedicated vector index type and the $vectorSearch operator; no separate vector store is required.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted LLMs of its own, but tight integrations and reference architectures with OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex for embedding and generation.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on Atlas managed clusters; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes billed by instance size/resources on top of standard Atlas cluster (compute/storage) pricing, consumption-based.
